raw_response: {"sentences":[{"text":"Leaving Bryant Park behind, we head for Times Square — about a twelve-minute walk.","source_id":"GLUE_NAV","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":4},{"text":"Before the lights hit, look back at the mile you've just walked.","source_id":"GLUE_REFLECTION","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":4},{"text":"At Grand Central, The Fisher King turned the Main Concourse into a ballroom of waltzing commuters.","source_id":"GLUE_REFLECTION","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":4},{"text":"At the Chrysler Building, William Van Alen hid a spire in an elevator shaft and raised it to 1,046 feet, beating his rival Severance by 117 feet.","source_id":"GLUE_REFLECTION","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":4},{"text":"At the library, two marble lions — Patience and Fortitude, named by Mayor LaGuardia in the 1930s — still keep watch.","source_id":"GLUE_REFLECTION","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":4},{"text":"And Bryant Park, a crime-ridden 'Needle Park' in the 1970s, is now where the city goes ice-skating.","source_id":"GLUE_REFLECTION","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":4},{"text":"The most famous square on earth started as a nobody — an unremarkable crossroads called Longacre Square.","source_id":"40cc5bb6-3fea-4168-8b33-6f672101cd82","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"What changed it was a deal between two ambitious men: August Belmont, building the city's first subway line from Lower Manhattan up to Harlem, and Adolph Ochs, publisher of the New York Times.","source_id":"40cc5bb6-3fea-4168-8b33-6f672101cd82","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"Belmont figured a Midtown business hub would fill his trains, so he pitched Ochs on moving the paper to Broadway and 42nd Street — an in-house station meant faster distribution and more sales to the flood of commuters.","source_id":"40cc5bb6-3fea-4168-8b33-6f672101cd82","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"Then he talked Mayor George B McClellan Jr into renaming the square for the broadsheet.","source_id":"40cc5bb6-3fea-4168-8b33-6f672101cd82","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"In the winter of 1904–05, both the subway station and the Times' new headquarters at One Times Square opened for business.","source_id":"40cc5bb6-3fea-4168-8b33-6f672101cd82","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"To celebrate, the Times threw a New Year's Eve party in 1904, firing fireworks off its rooftop.","source_id":"44ff8a13-ba96-4516-a533-c96b2fbbf8e5","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"By 1907 the square was so built up that those fireworks were ruled a hazard, and the paper needed a new crowd-puller.","source_id":"44ff8a13-ba96-4516-a533-c96b2fbbf8e5","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"The answer was a 700-pound wood-and-iron ball, lowered from the roof of One Times Square to welcome 1908.","source_id":"44ff8a13-ba96-4516-a533-c96b2fbbf8e5","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"Around a million people still crowd in every New Year's Eve to watch a Waterford crystal ball drop at midnight.","source_id":"44ff8a13-ba96-4516-a533-c96b2fbbf8e5","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"This is the New York of collective fantasies.","source_id":"9f4b17a2-2dcf-4dc1-8e3b-78f1e38605c7","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"It's where Al Jolson 'makes it' in the 1927 film The Jazz Singer, where Alfred Eisenstaedt caught a sailor kissing a nurse on V-J Day in 1945, and where Alicia Keys and Jay-Z sang about the concrete jungle.","source_id":"9f4b17a2-2dcf-4dc1-8e3b-78f1e38605c7","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"But the theater got here first.","source_id":"93861849-6a9e-419f-8658-56e60d4a076e","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"The neighborhood's first playhouse was the Empire, opened in 1893 on Broadway between 40th and 41st.","source_id":"93861849-6a9e-419f-8658-56e60d4a076e","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"Two years later a cigar manufacturer and part-time comedy writer named Oscar Hammerstein opened the Olympia, then in 1900 the Republic — today the children's theater New Victory.","source_id":"93861849-6a9e-419f-8658-56e60d4a076e","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"That set off a run of new venues, including the New Amsterdam and the Lyceum, both still going.","source_id":"93861849-6a9e-419f-8658-56e60d4a076e","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"Those early houses grew straight out of vaudeville, staging popular plays and suggestive comedies.","source_id":"f2e1657d-36e5-4e4f-80dc-65ef18308aa9","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"By the 1920s they'd swelled into full spectacles — lighthearted musicals like Show Boat, Hammerstein's epic about performers on a Mississippi steamboat, spinning off classics like Cole Porter's 'Let's Misbehave.'","source_id":"f2e1657d-36e5-4e4f-80dc-65ef18308aa9","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4,"also_cites":["93861849-6a9e-419f-8658-56e60d4a076e"]},{"text":"But the district was also becoming a launchpad for serious American drama.","source_id":"93861849-6a9e-419f-8658-56e60d4a076e","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"Its greatest early voice was Eugene O'Neill, born right here at the long-gone Barrett Hotel, 1500 Broadway.","source_id":"93861849-6a9e-419f-8658-56e60d4a076e","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"He debuted many of his plays on these stages, including the Pulitzer winners Beyond the Horizon and Anna Christie.","source_id":"93861849-6a9e-419f-8658-56e60d4a076e","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"Then, in 1943, Broadway landed its first runaway hit — Oklahoma!, which ran a record 2,212 performances.","source_id":"f2e1657d-36e5-4e4f-80dc-65ef18308aa9","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"O'Neill's success cleared the way for Tennessee Williams, Arthur Miller and Edward Albee, a legacy the Tony Awards began honoring in 1947.","source_id":"93861849-6a9e-419f-8658-56e60d4a076e","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"Today those shows play in one of 41 official Broadway theaters, lavish early-20th-century jewels ringing the square.","source_id":"f2e1657d-36e5-4e4f-80dc-65ef18308aa9","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"The whole scene got its own portrait in the 2014 Oscar-winner Birdman.","source_id":"f17a6dde-ff68-4c87-a98c-6c6f9bd413a2","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"A washed-up Michael Keaton is trying to stage a Broadway adaptation at the St James Theatre on West 44th, gets locked out, and ends up marching through Times Square in nothing but his underwear.","source_id":"f17a6dde-ff68-4c87-a98c-6c6f9bd413a2","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"A few blocks east, he spars over the play with Lindsay Duncan at the historic drinking den Rum House.","source_id":"f17a6dde-ff68-4c87-a98c-6c6f9bd413a2","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"And that brings our walk to a close.","source_id":"GLUE_CLOSING","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":4},{"text":"Thank you for coming along with me today — when you're ready, take your time and keep exploring on your own.","source_id":"GLUE_CLOSING","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":4}]}
